rules.statement: Don't ask to narrow a catch-all that translates every unexpected exception into the component's documented contract exception when the interface's contract says implementations fail only with that exception type.
rules.why: Narrowing it would let raw exceptions escape the interface contract. The catch-all is deliberate and pinned by tests.
rules.check: Before reporting, read the interface or adapter contract docs and the sibling implementations. If they require failing only with the domain exception, the catch-all is correct.

rules.statement: Don't ask to set HttpClient.Timeout to Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan on a client whose AddStandardResilienceHandler total timeout is shorter than the 100-second default client timeout.
rules.why: The pipeline's total timeout always fires first, so the client timeout never decides, and no rule asks for an infinite client timeout.
rules.check: Compare the configured resilience total timeout with HttpClient.Timeout. Report only if the total timeout is longer than the client timeout.

rules.statement: Don't report the use of Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience's AddStandardResilienceHandler on a named HttpClient as a violation that calls for a hand-written Polly.Core DelegatingHandler.
rules.why: The C# instructions name Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for bounded, jittered retries of outbound calls.
rules.check: Check the coding instructions' outbound-calls section before asking to swap the resilience package.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask to split a theory row into its own test when the row's input passes every check except the one under test.
rules.why: Such a row already isolates that check: removing the check makes only that row fail.
rules.check: Before reporting, ask whether the row's input could be refused for any reason other than the setting or check it targets.

rules.statement: Don't report as nested calls the calls that sit in string interpolations, in lambda bodies, as the receiver of a member call, in object or array creation expressions, or in a method chain. The hoist-into-a-local rule covers only calls passed directly as arguments to other calls.
rules.why: The hoisting convention exempts these forms, as applied consistently across the codebase.
rules.check: Report only a method call written directly as an argument of another call, outside those exempt forms.

rules.statement: Don't ask to rename an IServiceCollection variable or parameter named `services`, or a JsonElement that holds a parsed response's root and is named `document`.
rules.why: The C# and test instructions and existing code use `services`. A parsed response's root element is the document.
rules.check: Before reporting a naming issue, check that a written naming rule actually requires the other name.

rules.statement: Options validation for an outbound base address must refuse a URI that carries user info, as well as a URI that isn't an absolute https URL ending in a slash with no query or fragment.
rules.why: A URL with embedded credentials would otherwise pass start-up validation and send them on every request.
rules.check: Look at validators of Uri options for a UserInfo check alongside the scheme, query and fragment checks.

rules.statement: Don't ask an options validator to echo the refused value of a URL or other credential-bearing option in its failure message. Naming the configuration key is enough.
rules.why: A base address is exactly where a credential would sit, and echoing it would copy that credential into the start-up exception.
rules.check: Before asking for the value in a validation message, consider whether the option can contain secrets such as user info.

rules.statement: Don't ask to replace a bounded byte[] response body with a pooled IBufferWriter<byte> when every caller parses or hashes the whole document. Rent only the transient chunk buffer from ArrayPool<byte>.Shared.
rules.why: The body must be kept whole anyway, so the gain is a chunk buffer that is already pooled.
rules.check: Check whether the read is size-capped and its callers need the full body before reporting the byte[].

rules.statement: When logic is deliberately duplicated across independently versioned packages, mark each copy with a `// Copied on purpose` comment that names the other copies, and don't ask to merge the copies into a shared type.
rules.why: Independently versioned packages never share a type, and the comment keeps a fix from landing in only one copy.
rules.check: Look for duplicated helpers across packages that have no comment naming their twins. Don't suggest a shared helper across separately versioned packages.

rules.statement: Build options-validation failure messages from the same named constants the checks use, rather than repeating threshold literals in the message.
rules.why: A message written with a literal can drift from its check.
rules.check: Look for numbers or lengths in validator messages that duplicate the limit the code tests.

rules.statement: Don't ask to drop a null check on a non-nullable reference-type options property: a configure callback can set null at runtime. The validator should refuse null with a message naming the key, not coalesce it to a new default.
rules.why: Without the check, the validator would throw instead of naming the configuration key, and coalescing hides bad configuration.
rules.check: For options validators, check that null is refused with a keyed message rather than replaced by `?? []`.

rules.statement: When wrapping a caught exception such as JsonException, FormatException or CryptographicException in a domain exception, pass it as the inner exception.
rules.why: Otherwise diagnostic details such as the parser's line and byte position are lost.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks that throw a new exception built from the caught exception's message only.

rules.statement: In a test project, cover every branch of an exception-classification helper: an unexpected exception, each outage type, and each exception that must propagate unwrapped.
rules.why: If the clauses were reordered or dropped, bad data could be reported as an outage, or leak unwrapped, and no test would fail.
rules.check: Compare the catch or when clauses of the classifier with the tests that drive each one.

rules.statement: In a test project, pin each comparison boundary on both sides: a value exactly at the limit, a value just outside it, and the smallest accepted value of each validator bound.
rules.why: Otherwise flipping `<` to `<=`, or `>` to `>=`, leaves the suite green.
rules.check: For each new bound or range check, look for tests at the exact limit and just beyond it, not only far-away values.

rules.statement: In a test project, test a shared or deduplicated asynchronous fetch with concurrent callers: hold the stub's response behind a TaskCompletionSource, never a fixed delay, and assert a single request and the same result.
rules.why: Sequential calls never exercise the concurrent path, so a regression where each caller fetches would go unnoticed.
rules.check: Look for caches or single-flight code whose tests only make calls one after another, or that use Task.Delay to create overlap.

rules.statement: A fetch shared by several callers must run under its own timeout, not the first caller's CancellationToken. Each caller stops waiting with WaitAsync on its own token.
rules.why: Otherwise one caller's cancellation aborts the fetch that other callers are waiting on.
rules.check: Look for a cached or shared Task started with the triggering caller's cancellation token.

rules.statement: Don't ask a static class to move its static helpers ahead of its extension block. The statics-first member order applies to types that also have instance members.
rules.why: A static class has no instance members for its statics to precede.
rules.check: Before reporting member order, check whether the type has instance members.

rules.statement: Hash concatenated inputs with IncrementalHash, appending each part, instead of allocating an array just to concatenate them, and encode text straight into the destination writer or buffer.
rules.why: Temporary concatenation arrays and string-to-byte[] encodings are avoidable allocations on every call.
rules.check: Look for byte arrays built only to be hashed, and for Encoding.GetBytes(string) results that are copied straight on.

rules.statement: Have fixed-size cryptographic routines write into a caller-supplied Span<byte> with stackalloc'd blocks, rather than returning byte[] and allocating transient arrays.
rules.why: Transient arrays and ToArray copies add several allocations per call.
rules.check: Look for new byte[] temporaries, ToArray() copies and byte[] returns in hashing or expansion helpers whose sizes are fixed.

rules.statement: In a test project, put a comment above each group of standard test vectors that cites its source, such as the RFC appendix, along with the inputs.
rules.why: Without it, reviewers can't confirm that the expected bytes are the specification's, unedited.
rules.check: Look for hard-coded expected cryptographic outputs that have no provenance comment.

rules.statement: In a test project, exercise exceptional branches of a cryptographic algorithm, such as the zero input of a curve map, with an expected value taken from an independent implementation or the specification.
rules.why: A real input reaches such a branch with negligible probability, so only a direct test catches a regression in it.
rules.check: Look for special-case arms in crypto math that no test reaches.

rules.statement: In production code, an options validator for an outbound HTTP base address must not accept a URI that contains user info.
rules.why: Credentials embedded in a configured URL are sent on every request.
rules.check: Look at Uri option validators for a UserInfo.Length check.

rules.statement: Don't ask to replace a literal resilience or timeout setting with a named constant when the literal is used once, on the property that names it.
rules.why: The property name already names the value, so a constant adds nothing.
rules.check: Before reporting a magic number, check whether it is repeated, or used once on a self-describing property.
